East Africa Shortfall Advisor
Project report · November 2026 · prototype

East Africa crop shortfall advisor

A model that flags which crops, in which countries, are likely to yield more than 10% below their recent average. Built from an 8-record public-domain seed dataset, augmented with FAOSTAT yields and NASA POWER weather for 10 countries and 14 crops.

0.81ROC-AUC on unseen years (0.5 is chance)
58%of real shortfalls caught, up from 26% before class balancing
66% vs 7%shortfall rate in the Very high band against the Low band
4,131country-crop-years after cleaning, 1981 to 2024

Two findings limit how it should be used. Most of the model's skill comes from recent yield history, with weather adding little at national scale. The companion yield estimate does not beat a "same as last year" guess.

Is the model working?

The model was trained on 1981 to 2012 and tested on 2013 to 2024, 1,218 cases it never saw. 22% of those were shortfalls.

Higher bands contain steadily more real shortfalls, which is the behaviour a warning tool needs.

55% of warnings were right; 58% of shortfalls were caught.

What class balancing changed

Only 23% of training rows were shortfalls (670 against 2,243). Left alone, every model learned to say "normal" almost always. Five balancing strategies were compared across three model families; logistic regression with random undersampling was selected.

Where the skill comes from

The model mainly detects crops already in a slump or with unstable yields. Weather alone has modest skill. National averages smooth out local droughts, so sub-national data is the main route to improvement.

What the data showed

The seed dataset is 8 records

Four crops, one tree, one rainfall zone, one soil type and one water feature, all free text and unverified. It was parsed into crop profiles and checked against modern yields; it could not be used for training.

One variable at a time: imbalance and noise

Crops are unevenly represented and shortfall years are the minority class. Cleaning removed 305 carried-forward repeat values and 9 implausible jumps.

Pairs of variables: dry seasons raise shortfalls

Many variables together: three climate groups

How this can help

  • Early warning. Official yield statistics arrive a year or more late. A risk band at the end of the season points attention to the country-crop pairs most likely to disappoint.
  • Advisory agents. Tools built on the seed dataset gain a measured, testable signal alongside the historical notes.
  • Insurance and planning. Each risk band has a known hit rate, which is the starting point for pricing or for triggering a review.

Limits

  • Predictions are national averages and say nothing about a district or farm.
  • About 36% of FAOSTAT yield values used are estimates, which are smoother than reality.
  • Country weather is the mean of 4 to 6 farming locations, not a cropland-weighted average.
  • The risk score is not a calibrated probability; read it through the bands.
  • The yield estimate (468 kg/ha average error) is worse than repeating last year's yield (416 kg/ha).
  • The seed records remain unverified against their cited sources.

Code, data, the full analysis and a Streamlit app are in the GitHub repository WachiraChris/EA-Agricultural-Data-.
